answer: Over plain LAN HTTP you lose the full feature set: it runs online-only, without local encryption, and your traffic is unencrypted. Browsers restrict service workers, crypto, and programmatic clipboard access to secure contexts, so those are unavailable. Editing, indexing, queries, Space Lua, plugs, attachments, and local password login remain available.

Memory for: If I serve the PWA over plain HTTP on my LAN instead of HTTPS, what do I lose besides offline startup?
[1] PWA.md (What the PWA gives you)
  Limits: Offline startup requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost), a working service worker and previously cached application code. Plain LAN HTTP runs online-only. See [[TLS#LAN HTTP (no TLS)]]. Installing the PWA does not change these requirements. / Server-backed [[Search]], shell execution, remote sharing and external network APIs require a connection. Local page navigation, editing and queries over the client Object Index can work with cached data. Let the initial sync finish and test the pages and attachments you need before relying on offline access. Browser storage is not a backup.
[2] TLS.md (LAN HTTP (no TLS))
  #getting-started / While silverBullet works over plain HTTP on a LAN IP or hostname in online-only mode, _HTTPS_ enables the full feature set, including offline use and local encryption. This page documents a few deployment options. / > **note** Note / > This is a browser enforced restriction: browsers restrict service workers, crypto, and programmatic clipboard access to secure contexts. This is why the recommended deployment model is TLS, but SilverBullet will make a best effort to work without it.
  Enable HTTP/2 on your reverse proxy: Whichever reverse proxy you use, make sure it serves SilverBullet over HTTP/2. Over HTTP/1.1, browsers allow only six simultaneous connections per host, and SilverBullet’s service worker and sync engine can use all of them. When that happens, every request stalls: the client reports “Could not reach remote server, we’re offline or the server is down”, requests to `/.ping` time out, and pages load slowly from the local copy, even though the server itself is up. / * **Caddy** enables HTTP/2 by default, so the configuration above needs no changes. / * **nginx**: add `http2 on;` to the `server` block (nginx 1.25.1 and later), or use `listen 443 ssl http2;` on older versions. / * **Nginx Proxy Manager**: edit the proxy host, open the _SSL_ tab and enable _HTTP/2 Support_. / To check, run the following, which should print `2`: / ```shell
[3] Install/Network and Internet.md (Network and Internet)
  #getting-started / To access SilverBullet from another device, make the server reachable on your network. / On a local network, you can use plain HTTP in online-only mode. This requires a live connection to the server and leaves your traffic unencrypted. See [[TLS#LAN HTTP (no TLS)]] for the full list of limitations. / For access over the Internet, use [[TLS]] so your connection is encrypted and SilverBullet’s offline features work. / To set this up: / 1. Run the server following the [[Install]] instructions and make it reachable from the devices you want to use. / 2. Enable [[Authentication]]. / 3. Set up [[TLS]] for the full feature set, or use LAN HTTP with the limitations above.
Exact facts:
- [1] SilverBullet Server’s browser client is a [Progressive Web App](https://web.dev/progressive-web-apps/) (PWA). It can be installed in a standalone window and can read and edit cached content offline. [[Desktop]] is the native application, with files stored in local folders.
- [2] Open your server using its LAN address, for example `http://192.168.1.20:3000`. The server must listen on an address reachable from your LAN. Editing, indexing, queries, Space Lua, plugs, attachments, and local password login remain available.
